title: Advancing nutraceutical delivery through microencapsulation: hybrid systems, controlled release, and machine learning‐driven optimization
content:
Abstract

Bioactive constituents have strong potential for nutraceutical applications, but their use in functional products is often limited by poor stability, low water solubility, low bioavailability, degradation during processing and storage, and undesirable sensory properties. Microencapsulation can help overcome these limitations by protecting bioactive compounds and improving their delivery. However, the wide range of wall materials and encapsulation techniques makes it difficult to select the most suitable system for each application. This review critically evaluates microencapsulation strategies for nutraceutical constituents by examining the relationships between bioactive properties, wall materials, encapsulation techniques, release mechanisms, and functional performance. Current evidence shows that there is no single encapsulation technique that is suitable for all constituents. Successful encapsulation depends on compatibility between the bioactive compound, wall material, processing conditions, and the intended application. Conventional techniques, especially spray drying and freeze drying, remain widely used, while lipid-based carriers, structured emulsions, and emerging systems provide additional options for improving stability and delivery. However, industrial application may be limited by scale-up challenges, processing complexity, cost, regulatory requirements, and the lack of standardized evaluation methods. Machine learning also offers new opportunities for formulation optimization, release prediction, and process design, although its application remains at an early stage. Overall, future research should focus on rational material and process selection, scalable and sustainable technologies, and standardized performance assessment to support the development of effective and commercially practical nutraceutical delivery systems. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
